title: No Board discipline for legally protected reproductive or gender-affirming care
rule_summary: Under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 32, notwithstanding any general or special law to the contrary, no person, pharmacy or pharmacy department shall be subject to discipline by the Board, including the revocation, suspension or cancellation of the certificate of registration or reprimand, censure or monetary fine, for providing or assisting, including dispensing of medication, in the provision of reproductive health care services or gender-affirming health care services as defined in M.G.L. c. 12, s. 11I1/2, or for any judgment, discipline or other sanction arising from such health care services, if the services as provided would have been lawful and consistent with the code of professional conduct for pharmacists if they occurred entirely in the commonwealth. The Board also shall not take adverse action on an application for registration of a qualified pharmacist based on a criminal or civil action or disciplinary action by a licensing board of another state that arises from such health care services, including the dispensing of medication, that, as provided, would have been lawful and consistent with that code if they occurred entirely in the commonwealth.
exam_relevance: Tests the statutory counterpart to 247 CMR 3.05: the bar reaches Board discipline itself as well as applications, and it holds only where the services would have been lawful and consistent with the pharmacist code of professional conduct had they occurred entirely in Massachusetts.

authority.name: Massachusetts General Laws
authority.section: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 32, first paragraph, provisos

common_confusions: The protection is conditional: the services must have been lawful and consistent with the code of professional conduct for pharmacists had they occurred entirely in the commonwealth.
verification_notes: Read in the current text of M.G.L. c. 112, s. 32 on malegislature.gov on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed. A fresh independent audit is still required before any section relying on it is published.
